bull.b: A debt-free balance sheet reduces borrowing-related financial risk and preserves flexibility while Coya funds clinical development. Avoiding interest obligations can help the company direct available resources toward trials and partnerships rather than debt servicing.

Completing enrollment in the 120-patient randomized, placebo-controlled ALSTARS study is a meaningful execution milestone. It supports a defined path toward topline data and reduces enrollment uncertainty for Coya’s lead ALS program.

The open-label extension can provide longer-term efficacy and safety observations while allowing participants to continue treatment. Combined with the stated cash runway, this supports continued development through the expected ALS data readout.

bear.b: Consistently negative operating and free cash flow indicate that Coya is not yet funding operations internally. Continued clinical investment therefore requires cash reserves or external funding, increasing financial pressure if development costs remain elevated.

The company’s substantial operating and net losses show that reported top-line momentum has not translated into a sustainable earnings model. Persistent losses can constrain reinvestment capacity and make progress toward self-funded growth dependent on future financing.

Deferring the FTD Phase 2 trial concentrates near-term development activity on ALS and delays clinical validation in another targeted disease. This narrows the pipeline’s near-term diversification and extends the wait for additional program-level evidence.
